acceptance.output_evidence: THE AND-CLAUSE, READ FOR DISCRIMINATION: YES for the refuse-then-admit pair this cell was asked to exercise. A copied 'official account of <domain>' bio is check3 alone; under official := (check1 OR check2) AND (any further evidence), check3 alone leaves check1 and check2 both False, so evaluate_official_vs_impostor returns status 'impostor' -- REFUSED, never official on the forgeable check by itself (exercised: test_impostor_account_passing_only_check3_is_refused, PASS). An account carrying the SAME copied bio (check3=True) but ALSO linked from the company's own measured web presence (check1=True) or carrying the platform's own verification mark (check2=True) is ADMITTED official (exercised: test_official_account_passing_check3_and_check1_is_admitted, PASS both halves). The refuse-then-admit pair genuinely turns on check1/check2, not on check3 -- the exact discrimination the L10 analysis asked for ('require check3 to CO-OCCUR with check1 OR check2'). RESIDUAL, DISCLOSED NOT HIDDEN (carried over unchanged from AMGT-s-15's own AC6 judgment row -- this cell's remit is the AND-clause only, not a re-audit of check1/check2's individual strength): (a) check1 (company web presence linking to the account) is currently UNUSABLE for all 89 names in AMGT-s-12's universe.json, because no ir_domain has resolved yet (G-24) -- until AMGT-s-4/-b4 resolve at least one, the only practical route to OFFICIAL for a real handle is check2. (b) check2 itself reads stronger in the schema's prose than it now is in practice: on at least one major platform, paid verification has been decoupled from identity verification since 2023, and neither the schema nor this cell's fix names that caveat -- it is out of the AND-clause's stated scope, flagged here rather than silently left unread. (c) The AND-clause closes the SPECIFIC exploit FWD-14 named (check3-alone admission) precisely and testably; it does not, and was not asked to, make check2 a strong signal again -- an impostor holding a paid verification mark and a copied bio would still pass (check2 OR check1) AND (further evidence) under today's rule, because check2 is trusted at face value. That is a different, disclosed gap, not this cell's remit. CONCLUSION: the AND-clause as built is the correct, minimal, testable fix to the one defect FWD-14 named, verified by the refuse-then-admit fixture pair; it does not fix check2's separately-weakened trust level.
